qwen3.6-coder.note: gguf incompatible with installed llama-server build 10155 (re-checked after upgrading from b9949 - same error persists, confirming this needs the file re-converted, not a newer/older runtime): 'qwen35moe.rope.dimension_sections has wrong array length; expected 4, got 3'. Needs re-quantizing with a matching llama.cpp version.

fable-fusion-27b.note: Community merge (DavidAU Fable-Fusion-711, dense 27B, uncensored/abliterated), not an official Qwen release. Now used for Open WebUI chat + custom Tools (data fetch/analysis), not coding. Tested: tool-calling works (stream+non-stream), MTP draft acceptance ~78-86%, but raw speed is only ~26 tok/s vs ~74 tok/s on qwen3.6-mtp (dense 27B costs far more per token than the sparse 35B-A3B MoE despite fewer total params). Context ceiling tested by hand: 65536 fits safely (~4.8GB headroom), 98304 triggered an internal CUDA OOM once (auto-recovered by retrying without pipeline parallelism, but left under 800MB free on one card) - not safe for real use, pinned to 65536 instead of trusting --fit's over-conservative 8192 default. Stress-tested tool-calling at temp=1.0 with a tight 400-token budget: 5/5 succeeded (unlike qwen3.6-mtp, which had real failures at its default temp before being lowered to 0.6) - so temperature was NOT overridden here, it's genuinely reliable as-is. --reasoning-budget/--no-reasoning-preserve added anyway as cheap insurance for long chat sessions, same reasoning as the coding profiles. Vision added afterward: unlike the original Unsloth qwen3.6-mtp model (whose card explicitly says MTP + --mmproj aren't supported together, why qwen3.6-main/qwen3.6-mtp are split), this DavidAU merge loads BOTH --spec-type draft-mtp and --mmproj together with no conflict - verified: vision test image correctly described AND MTP draft acceptance still ~82% simultaneously. VRAM headroom is tighter with vision loaded (~28.5GB/32GB used, ~3.8GB free) but stable, no OOM.

muse-glimmer-30b.note: Official Meta Superintelligence Lab release, dense 29.6B with a ViT-G/14 perception encoder, purpose-built for local agentic tasks - not a Qwen derivative. Needed a llama.cpp upgrade to load at all: the 'muse-glimmer' architecture wasn't recognized on b10155 (this model card's release date is Aug 2026, support merged into llama.cpp on 2026-08-10, PR #26841) - upgraded to b10355 to get it. Uses DFlash speculative decoding (block-of-16 drafter, separate --spec-draft-model file) instead of MTP, confirmed active via 'adding speculative implementation draft-dflash' in the log. Controls reasoning depth via a 'Reasoning strength: <low|medium|high|xhigh>' line in the system prompt rather than a CLI flag, so --reasoning-budget/--no-reasoning-preserve were deliberately not copied from other profiles. TESTED RESULTS: tool-calling reliable (8/8 across two batches, including a tight 400-token stress test - no reasoning-runaway issue). Vision works (mmproj loads fine alongside DFlash, no MTP-style conflict). But raw speed is only ~30-34 tok/s with DFlash active - SLOWER than qwen3.6-mtp's ~72-74 tok/s, and nowhere near the model card's claimed 3.1x/233 tok/s DFlash speedup, which was measured on an RTX 5090 (far more compute than this RTX 5060 Ti x2 setup) - marketing numbers from different hardware class did not transfer. --fit auto-picked only 8192 ctx despite ~12GB VRAM headroom being free; tested by hand instead: 131072 (matching the other main profiles) fits comfortably with ~10.3GB headroom to spare, thanks to the model's sliding-window attention (only 1 layer in 4 is 'Global', rest are 2048-window local) costing far less than Fable-Fusion's fully dense attention did. Benchmarks on the model card compare against Qwen3.6-27B specifically (not the 35B-A3B-MoE this setup actually runs day to day) with mixed results - wins agentic/tool benchmarks like MCP Atlas, loses coding-specific ones like TerminalBench/OSWorld/SWE-Bench Verified. Net: works correctly, but not faster than the current setup on this hardware - kept as a profile to try for its native tool-recovery/reasoning-strength design, not adopted as default. IMPORTANT: this profile uses Unsloth's OWN independent GGUF conversion (UD-Q4_K_XL, ~14.8GB) - see 'muse-glimmer-30b-meta' below for Meta's own official kquant-dynamic export (19.7GB), a genuinely different quantization pipeline, not the same file despite both being '4-bit-class'.

muse-glimmer-30b-meta.note: Meta's OWN official GGUF export (huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF) - this is the literal file the model card's 0.2%-degradation/32GB-VRAM 'K-Quant-Dynamic' claim refers to, confirmed by filename (muse-glimmer-30B-kquant-dynamic.gguf) and exact byte-size match against the repo's own listing. Different quantization pipeline from Unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL above (19.7GB vs ~14.8GB for the same nominal '4-bit' tier) - reuses the same dflash-kquant.gguf/mmproj-kquant.gguf companion files since those are byte-identical between both repos (verified via content-length before downloading only the ~18.3GB text model). TESTED HEAD-TO-HEAD vs the Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL profile above: tool-calling reliable (8/8 across two batches incl. tight-budget stress test, identical result), vision works identically ('a blue circle'), speed/draft-acceptance statistically indistinguishable (27.7-34.7 tok/s, ~54-67% acceptance vs Unsloth's 27.7-34.3 tok/s, ~54-69%) - the larger, more-precise Meta weights did NOT measurably change speed or reliability on this hardware. ctxSize 131072 hand-tested and fits, but with less headroom than Unsloth's variant (~6.8GB free vs ~10.3GB) since the weights alone are ~5GB bigger. Net: no observed practical difference between the two quantizations in this setup's actual usage (tool-calling, vision, speed) despite Meta's official 0.2% vs unknown/unverified degradation numbers - the quality gap this claims to close may only show up in evals this setup can't run, not in casual use.

qwen3.6-27b.note: Official Qwen (Alibaba) dense 27B, plain (no MTP) - the actual model the Muse Glimmer card's 'Qwen3.6-27B Thinking Mode' benchmark comparisons refer to, which this setup never directly tested until now (Fable-Fusion is a DavidAU uncensored merge of the same base, not the pristine original). Same sampling as qwen3.6-mtp/qwen3.6-main for direct comparability. Vision added (mmproj-F16, shared with the MTP profile - byte-identical between both Unsloth repos) and verified: correctly described the test image.

qwen3.6-27b-mtp.note: Official Qwen dense 27B with MTP - lets us isolate MTP's speedup contribution on a DENSE architecture (vs the sparse MoE qwen3.6-mtp) and compare against the dense+MTP Fable-Fusion merge's numbers (~26-34 tok/s, ~78-86% draft acceptance) using the pristine, uncensored-merge-free original this time. Vision added (same mmproj as qwen3.6-27b) and verified working TOGETHER with MTP (81% draft acceptance in the same vision request, no conflict) - same pleasant surprise Fable-Fusion had; only the original 35B-A3B qwen3.6-mtp documents MTP+mmproj as incompatible.

qwen3.8-27b.note: Official Unsloth GGUF of the newest Qwen point release (Qwen3.8-27B, dense, architecture foundation is Qwen3.5 not Qwen3.6 - a hybrid design: 16 groups of [3x(Gated DeltaNet linear-attention -> FFN) + 1x(Gated full-attention -> FFN)], so only 16 of 64 layers carry a real KV cache, the rest use a cheap recurrent DeltaNet state - similar memory-efficiency idea to Muse Glimmer's sliding-window design. Native context 262144 (extensible to 1M via YaRN). Originally tried UD-Q6_K_XL (25.9GB) at the user's request for the higher-precision tier, but that hit a hard CUDA OOM at 131072 ctx allocating the mmproj buffer (only fit at 65536). User then asked which quant would preserve the most capability while still fitting the full 131072 ctx used by every other 27B profile - estimated from the Q6 failure's headroom math that UD-Q5_K_XL should fit with several GB to spare, downloaded it (20.2GB) and confirmed: loads cleanly at 131072 with ~2.1-3.5GB free per GPU. Bonus: Q5_K_XL is also faster than Q6_K_XL was (~16.85 tok/s vs ~13.8 tok/s unaccelerated) - smaller quant, less compute per token. --fit could not help either quant ('n_gpu_layers already set by user to 999, abort'), so this ctxSize was hand-verified, not auto-picked. Sampling taken from the model's own card: thinking-mode temp=1.0/top_p=0.95/top_k=20/min_p=0.0/presence_penalty=0.0 (used here); card also lists an instruct/non-thinking alternative (temp=0.7/top_p=0.80/presence_penalty=1.5) not used since this setup runs thinking mode like all other profiles. TESTED at Q5_K_XL/131072: tool-calling 8/8 (3x generous 1024-budget + 5x tight 400-budget, all succeeded - card advertises 'tool calling improvements: parsing nested objects' and this held up). Vision verified (mmproj-F16 correctly described the standard test image). Discovery while inspecting the load log: this GGUF's tensor list includes 'blk.64.nextn.*' (MTP head) tensors that get silently ignored/unused without --spec-type - i.e. MTP is baked into this SAME file, unlike Qwen3.6-27B which needed a separately-published '-MTP-GGUF' repo. See qwen3.8-27b-mtp below, which enables it on this identical file with zero extra download.

qwen3.8-27b-mtp.note: Same file as qwen3.8-27b (Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q5_K_XL.gguf) with --spec-type draft-mtp added - this base GGUF has its MTP head baked in (blk.64.nextn.* tensors, confirmed active via 'creating MTP draft context against the target model' in the startup log), so this needed no separate download, just the extra flag. Loads cleanly at the full 131072 ctxSize (~1.8-2.1GB/GPU free, slightly tighter than the non-MTP profile's ~2.1-3.5GB since the MTP head itself takes some VRAM). TESTED at 131072: tool-calling 3/3 and vision both verified working together with MTP active (no conflict, consistent with every other dense Qwen3.6/Fable-Fusion profile in this setup - only the original 35B-A3B qwen3.6-mtp documents MTP+mmproj as incompatible). Speed: ~28-30 tok/s vs ~16.85 tok/s without MTP (~1.7x), draft acceptance 77-79% (e.g. 217/276 accepted, mean accepted run length ~2.5-2.6) - both speed and acceptance came out even better than the earlier Q6_K_XL/65536 test (24.5 tok/s, 72% acceptance), so the lighter quant was a net win on every axis (fits full context, faster, and no worse - actually better - draft acceptance). Net: still well below qwen3.6-mtp's ~74 tok/s (sparse MoE - the recurring finding in this setup remains that MoE sparsity beats dense+MTP on this hardware), but MTP is a clear, free win over the plain qwen3.8-27b profile if this model is the one in use.
